concepts.name: Pronunciation and spelling rules
concepts.summary: Recall the regular letter-to-sound mapping, including rolled r, c as 'ch', ng, ny, and stress that is light and near-even.

concepts.name: Greetings and polite formulas
concepts.summary: Understand and use time-of-day greetings (selamat pagi, siang, sore, malam) and courtesy words like terima kasih, maaf, tolong and silakan.

concepts.name: Personal pronouns and address
concepts.summary: Understand the difference between saya, aku, kamu, Anda and kinship or title address like Bapak and Ibu in choosing formality.

concepts.name: Basic SVO sentence order
concepts.summary: Build simple subject-verb-object sentences where verbs take no conjugation and no tense marking.

concepts.name: Copula-free equational sentences
concepts.summary: Understand that predicates like adjectives and nouns follow the subject without 'to be', with adalah only optional before nouns.

concepts.name: Question words and yes-no questions
concepts.summary: Form questions with apa, siapa, di mana, kapan, berapa and the particle apakah.

concepts.name: Numbers and basic negation
concepts.summary: Recall numbers 1 to 1000 and choose between tidak for verbs and adjectives and bukan for nouns.

misconceptions.text: Indonesian verbs change form to show past, present and future.
Tidak and bukan are interchangeable words for 'not'.
Anda is the normal word for 'you' in everyday conversation with anyone.

concepts.name: Time markers sudah, belum, akan
concepts.summary: Apply sudah, belum, sedang and akan to express completion, non-completion, ongoing action and future as optional aspect markers.

concepts.name: Noun-adjective order and possession
concepts.summary: Form phrases with the head noun first, such as rumah besar and buku saya, and use yang for modifiers.

concepts.name: Classifiers buah, orang, ekor
concepts.summary: Apply the right classifier after a number, such as dua orang, tiga ekor, lima buah, when counting objects.

concepts.name: Market and shopping dialogue
concepts.summary: Use phrases for prices, quantities and bargaining, such as berapa harganya, boleh kurang, and mahal.

concepts.name: Travel and directions phrases
concepts.summary: Ask for and follow directions and transport using lurus, kiri, kanan, dekat, jauh, and place prepositions di, ke, dari.

concepts.name: Base verbs and the prefix ber-
concepts.summary: Understand and form common intransitive ber- verbs for having, doing or using, such as bekerja, berjalan and bermain.

concepts.name: Reduplication for plurals
concepts.summary: Understand reduplication such as buku-buku and use it appropriately, noting it is unnecessary after a quantity word.

misconceptions.text: Sudah means 'past tense' and must be used for every past event.
Classifiers can be dropped or swapped freely, so buah works for people and animals.
Plurals always need reduplication, even after numbers like tiga.

concepts.name: Active prefix meN- and its variants
concepts.summary: Apply the meN- prefix with its sound changes (mem-, men-, meny-, meng-, menge-) and dropping of initial k, p, t, s.

concepts.name: Passive di- and object-fronted passive
concepts.summary: Form di- passives with an agent introduced by oleh, and the pronoun-verb passive like buku itu saya baca.

concepts.name: Prefix ter- meanings
concepts.summary: Distinguish ter- as accidental or already-completed state, ability, and superlative, as in terbuka and tercepat.

concepts.name: Nominalising circumfix pe-an and peN-
concepts.summary: Analyse nouns formed by pe-an, per-an, peN- and ke-an to tell process, doer and result apart.

concepts.name: Suffix -kan causative and benefactive
concepts.summary: Analyse how -kan makes a causative or benefactive verb, as in membersihkan and membelikan.

concepts.name: Suffix -i locative and repetitive
concepts.summary: Analyse how -i marks a location target or repeated action, as in menduduki and mendatangi.

concepts.name: Relative clauses with yang
concepts.summary: Build relative and nominalised clauses with yang and conjunctions such as karena, supaya and kalau.

misconceptions.text: Me- is a single fixed prefix with the same spelling on every root.
-kan and -i are interchangeable and give the same meaning on any verb.
Ter- always means 'most' like a superlative.

concepts.name: Choosing between -kan and -i
concepts.summary: Analyse minimal pairs such as menanami versus menanamkan and mengirimi versus mengirimkan to select the correct argument structure.

concepts.name: Register and formal versus colloquial
concepts.summary: Evaluate formal baku usage against colloquial forms such as nggak, gue, ngomong and drop of prefixes to fit the context.

concepts.name: Stacked affixation and word derivation
concepts.summary: Analyse complex derived words such as mempertanggungjawabkan, memperbaiki and keberlangsungan into root and layers.

concepts.name: Prefix memper- and its effect
concepts.summary: Analyse memper- forms like memperbesar and mempelajari for causation, intensification and added valency.

concepts.name: Discourse connectors and cohesion
concepts.summary: Evaluate the use of connectors such as meskipun, sehingga, padahal and oleh karena itu to structure paragraphs.

concepts.name: Loanwords and borrowed vocabulary
concepts.summary: Analyse borrowings from Dutch, Arabic, Sanskrit and English and their adapted spelling in formal writing.

concepts.name: Passive choice and topic focus
concepts.summary: Evaluate when to use active, di- or fronted-agent passive to manage topic, definiteness and politeness.

misconceptions.text: Colloquial Jakarta speech is simply wrong Indonesian and should never be used.
The passive is rare and merely a stylistic variant of the active.
Any root can take any affix combination to form a real word.

concepts.name: Writing in varied registers
concepts.summary: Create texts such as reports, speeches and informal messages that apply the register, affixation and cohesion fitting each genre.

concepts.name: Regional language influence
concepts.summary: Evaluate how Javanese, Betawi and Malay varieties shape Indonesian grammar, vocabulary and speech practices.

concepts.name: Evaluating usage norms
concepts.summary: Evaluate usage against EYD or PUEBI and KBBI norms and judge when divergence is acceptable.

concepts.name: Creating neologisms with affixes
concepts.summary: Create and justify new terms using productive affixes and compounding consistent with the language's morphology.

concepts.name: Translating between English and Indonesian
concepts.summary: Produce translations that handle missing tense, definiteness, classifiers and pronoun choice without calquing English.

concepts.name: Pragmatics and politeness strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate address terms, indirectness and face-saving strategies in negotiation, hierarchy and cross-cultural settings.

misconceptions.text: Good Indonesian translation follows English word order and tense one to one.
There is a single correct standard that all speakers follow in every context.
Formal pronoun Anda is always the safest and most polite choice.
